credential_rules: Authorization Bearer/Basic and standalone Bearer-shaped values; recognizable GitHub/GitLab/GoogleAPI/AWS/Slack/OpenAI tokens and JWT shapes.
Nonempty API-key/access-token/refresh-token/client-secret/secret-key/password/passwd/pwd assignments, credential-bearing HTTP URL user:password forms.
Additional auth/session/id/OAuth token, AWS secret-access-key, WiFi password/PSK and GoogleOAuth value shapes.
No candidate credential bytes or surrounding secret values are copied into reports; an actual hit would be reported only by file/byte offset/LF and rule.
artifact_and_content_rules: Selected paths must remain inside the repository, be regular non-symlink files and at most8MiB; all stored selection SHA256/lengths and final read hashes were checked.
Rejected unexpected boot magic, ARM64 Image magic, Android/vendor boot headers, database/DEX/ZIP bodies and Image/vmlinux/ramdisk/boot-image filenames; no such selected artifacts found.
Exactly three user-authorized small ET_REL AArch64 KO files are allowed by exact path, SHA256 and size for offline GPI/SPI disassembly. No general KO/executable exception is granted.
Checked raw binary/text bytes, one bounded standalone gzip kernel configuration, and532 named JSON*_hex metadata fields (258630decoded bytes).

Searched page-sized contiguous address-labelled hexdump runs and long hex strings. Five decoded fields>=4KiB were individually attributed to recorded cat /proc/modules or cat /proc/mounts commands; they are ordinary textual metadata, not backing-page dumps.

File inventory consists of selected kernel/Android diagnostic logs, state/audit metadata, GNU notes, command lines, config and reference C/patch/disassembly plus the three explicit modules. No application database, media, message archive or protected backing-memory dump was selected or identified.

limits: This is a bounded content review of the three exact selection manifests, not the whole repository, Git history, remote service or files only mentioned as references.

Pattern and format checks plus targeted metadata-origin review cannot prove absence of every secret or personal detail in all free-form logs. Arbitrary obfuscation, encryption, damaged bytes and unknown token formats are not decoded or repaired.

Ordinary logs may contain device identifiers, technical paths, package/process names, addresses and hashes; these are intentionally retained by the user request. Such metadata is not treated as a credential or application-data payload.

Full forensic binaries are limited to the three explicitly authorized small modules. Their presence is evidence for offline review, not an installation/execute recommendation or proof of runtime adoption.
The review is a hash-bound snapshot, not an atomic lock of all files. Copy/export must preserve original bytes and verify these SHA256 values again; this report does not cover later edits.
No raw characters were repaired, and no protected memory was read. No device, build, test, git or network action was performed.

Final package additions were scanned only once as11 small build/selection metadata files. The older688 content was not rescanned in this supplement; package manifest length/SHA records were compared to the existing scanned inventory. This audit does not perform Git publication or claim a remote upload occurred.
